findings.title: Backup code login rejected for SAML/Google users with 2FA
findings.body: The guard `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode) throw new Error(ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled)` (and the similar password check below at line 117) only exempts requests carrying a totpCode. When a user whose identity provider is Google/SAML has 2FA enabled and tries to log in with a backup code (totpCode empty, backupCode set — exactly what the new 'Lost access' flow submits via the `?totp=` JWT login page), they hit this branch first and get 'account created with identity provider' instead of reaching the new backup-code verification below. Backup codes are therefore unusable for precisely the IdP users the external-TOTP login flow serves; the checks must also allow `credentials.backupCode`.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a check-then-update race, allowing code reuse
findings.body: The authorize callback decrypts the backup code list, checks `indexOf`, and then issues a separate `prisma.user.update` to mark the code used. Two concurrent login attempts with the same backup code can both pass the `indexOf` check before either update commits, so a single-use code can be redeemed twice. Since the codes are short (40 bits of entropy) and the rate limiter is the only mitigation, the consumption should be atomic (e.g., conditional update inside a transaction, or re-read-and-verify within a serializable transaction).

findings.title: First 2FA test never closes the new backup-codes screen, so the enabled-switch assertion is unreliable
findings.body: After the PR, successful TOTP submission shows the DisplayBackupCodes step instead of closing the modal. The first test ('should allow a user to enable 2FA and login using 2FA') was not updated: it goes straight to asserting the `two-factor-switch` state while the backup-code dialog is still open, and the PR itself adds a FIXME noting this assertion 'passes even when switch is not checked'. The test should click `backup-codes-close` (like the disable test does) and then assert on `[data-state="checked"]`; as written it no longer proves that enabling 2FA worked.

findings.title: Unvalidated req.body.backupCode can crash the disable endpoint
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes the client sent a string. The request body is not validated, so a non-string value (e.g. a number or object) causes a TypeError and a 500 instead of a 400 IncorrectBackupCode. Coerce/validate the body (e.g. zod) before use, as is done elsewhere in the codebase.
